# Results — Study 865 (Credit → Equity Lead-Lag)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test:
**"credit leads equity"** — the trailing 1-4-week duration-hedged high-yield credit return
(HYG in excess of IEF) is said to *turn before* stocks, so it should **predict the next
week's SPY return** (a Granger-style lead-lag). Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `c6ce5a5566a2`
(the four-ETF daily close panel).*

Data as-of 2026-06-30. Fingerprint `c6ce5a5566a2`.

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily total-return closes (`auto_adjust=True`) for **HYG, IEF, LQD, SPY**, 2007-05-01 → 2026-06-30, **4,822** daily rows → **1,001** Friday-anchored weekly closes |
| Signal | **credit trend** = trailing-`k`-week total return of HYG **minus** IEF (duration-hedged), `k = 4` weeks as the headline, `k = 1, 2` weeks as cross-checks; known at the close of week `t` |
| Test | **predictive regression** `r_SPY[t+1] = a + b·trend_k[t] + u` — next-week SPY return on the trailing HY-excess trend (Granger-style one-step lead), Newey-West *t* on the slope `b`; plus a companion risk-on/off discrimination on next-week SPY |
| Timing rule | `risk_on = 1{trend > 0}` at week `t` → hold **SPY** over week `t+1`; else hold **IEF**. Benchmark = 100%-SPY buy-and-hold |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: trend through the close of week `t` → position held over week `t+1`. A SPY↔IEF switch turns the book over (sell one, buy the other = **2 legs**), charged `cost_bps` one-way each × NAV on the switch week; long-only, no borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, Bartlett, 6-lag) *t* on the regression slope and on the risk-on−risk-off difference (via a time-ordered regime-contrast series); a Welch *t*; a 1,000-draw label-shift placebo; a two-era cut; a Newey-West *t* on the overlay's weekly active return; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** HYG, IEF, LQD and SPY are all live,
continuously-listed ETFs, so the *tape* carries **no delisting bias**. The Signal-axis
caveat is different and just as real: this is **one** US credit history (2007-2026,
essentially a single realised path through the GFC, the 2015-16 HY wobble, COVID and the
2022 sell-off). A weekly lead-lag fit on one regime path is exposed to single-sample
overfit; the era split below is the honesty check.

## The signal — does the credit trend LEAD next-week equity?

We regress the *next* week's SPY return on the trailing-`k`-week HY-excess trend known at
the close of week `t`. If credit genuinely leads equity, the slope `b` should be **positive
and robust** (a rising credit trend → a higher SPY return the following week).

| horizon | slope `b` | SPY move per 1σ trend | NW(6) *t* | R² | corr |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **4-week (headline), n = 996** | **−0.0546** | **−19.6 bps** | **−1.70** | 0.60% | −0.078 |
| 1-week cross-check | −0.1073 | −19.5 bps | −1.58 | 0.59% | −0.077 |
| 2-week cross-check | −0.0117 | −2.9 bps | −0.23 | 0.01% | −0.012 |

The claimed lead **does not appear** — and what little there is points the **wrong way**.
At the headline 4-week horizon the slope is **negative** (a stronger trailing credit trend
precedes a *lower* next-week SPY return: −19.6 bps per one-σ trend), with a Newey-West
*t* of just **−1.70** — shy of significance and, crucially, the *opposite* sign to the
"credit leads equity" story (it is a faint one-week **mean-reversion**, not a lead). The
1-week trend agrees (−19.5 bps, *t* = −1.58); the 2-week horizon is flat. The R² never
exceeds 0.6% — credit explains essentially none of next week's stocks.

## Discrimination — risk-on vs risk-off next-week SPY (4-week trend)

Split next-week SPY by the sign of the trailing credit trend — the exact quantity the
timing overlay earns:

| group | next-week SPY | n |
|---|--:|--:|
| risk-on weeks (trend > 0), 58.2% | **+19.5 bps** | 580 |
| risk-off weeks (trend ≤ 0) | **+27.0 bps** | 416 |
| **difference (on − off)** | **−7.5 bps/week** (NW *t* = **−0.48**, Welch *t* = −0.43) | |

Again wrong-signed and negligible: risk-on (positive-trend) weeks earned a *lower* next-week
SPY return than risk-off weeks. Conditioning on the credit trend adds no forward
discrimination.

## Placebo — is the (tiny, wrong-sign) difference distinguishable from noise?

Keep the next-week SPY series but **circularly shift** the risk-on labels by a random offset
(breaks the lead→outcome link, preserves autocorrelation and the risk-on share), 1,000 draws
(20 seeds × 50):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed difference | **−7.5 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | −0.2 bps (16.2) |
| position of observed | ≈ **−0.4σ** (right-tail p = 0.663) |

The observed −7.5 bps sits **inside** the placebo cloud (−0.4σ, p = 0.66): the credit-trend
labelling carries no information a random relabelling doesn't. There is nothing to explain.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2017-01-01), regression slope

| era | slope `b` | NW *t* | R² |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2007-01 → 2017-01 (n=501) | **−0.0439** | −1.23 | 0.53% |
| 2017-01 → 2026-06 (n=495) | **−0.0910** | −1.33 | 0.90% |

The slope is **wrong-signed in both halves** and clears |*t*| ≥ 2 in neither. The sign is at
least *consistent* (both negative) — this is not a sign-flipping accident but a persistent,
statistically weak *anti*-lead: over this sample credit's recent strength mildly foreshadows
equity giving a little back, the reverse of the folk claim, and too weak to trade.

## The overlay — can the SPY↔IEF switch beat buy-and-hold?

`risk_on` → SPY next week, else IEF, costed; compared to a 100%-SPY buy-and-hold. 218
switches over 19 years (≈11/yr).

| one-way cost | net Sharpe | B&H Sharpe | net CAGR | B&H CAGR | net maxDD | B&H maxDD | active/wk | active NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp/leg** | **0.644** | 0.645 | +7.35% | +10.61% | −32.7% | −54.6% | −7.6 bps | **−1.22** |
| **5 bps/leg** | 0.569 | 0.645 | +6.37% | +10.61% | −33.3% | −54.6% | −9.3 bps | −1.49 |

The overlay's **only** real benefit is a shallower drawdown (−33% vs −55%): sitting in IEF
through risk-off stretches dodges some of the worst equity air-pockets. But it is **not an
edge**. Even at a generous 1 bp/leg the net Sharpe (0.644) is a statistically insignificant
hair *below* buy-and-hold (0.645) — the weekly active return is *negative* (−7.6 bps/week,
NW *t* = −1.22) — and by a realistic 5 bps/leg it falls to 0.569. On raw return the overlay
forfeits **3.3%/yr of CAGR** (7.4% vs 10.6%) by parking in bonds during the 2010s bull. It is
drawdown *insurance you pay for in forgone return*, not a lead-lag premium.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded panel with a persistent latent risk-on factor that drives the
duration-hedged credit trend and (with `edge > 0`) the SPY return **one trading week later**
— a genuine planted lead. No network.

| world | regression NW *t* | overlay vs B&H |
|---|--:|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.26** (sd 0.75), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** | — |
| planted (`edge = 0.02`, seed 865) | **+26.7** (per-σ +988 bps, R² 76%) | active NW *t* = **+6.90**, overlay Sharpe +3.81 vs B&H +0.19 |

The detector never fires on the null and cleanly recovers a *planted* one-week lead of credit
over equity — so the flat, wrong-signed real-tape result is a genuine absence, not a broken
engine. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape
stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The credit trend (HYG excess over IEF) does **not** lead next-week
  equity. The predictive-regression slope is **wrong-signed and insignificant** at every
  horizon (4-week −19.6 bps/σ, NW *t* = **−1.70**; 1-week *t* = −1.58; 2-week *t* = −0.23),
  the R² never exceeds 0.6%, the risk-on−risk-off difference sits **inside** a label-shift
  placebo (−0.4σ, p = 0.66), and the wrong sign is **consistent across eras** (both halves
  negative, |*t*| < 2). A clean 20-seed synthetic control recovers a *planted* lead, so the
  flat result is a true absence. If anything, credit's recent strength faintly foreshadows
  equity *mean-reverting* — the reverse of the claim, and untradeable.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The weekly SPY↔IEF overlay never beats buy-and-hold: net Sharpe
  0.644 vs 0.645 at 1 bp/leg is an insignificant hair *below* the benchmark (active NW *t* =
  **−1.22**, active return *negative*), it forfeits **3.3%/yr of CAGR**, and by 5 bps/leg its
  Sharpe (0.569) falls further behind. Its one honest merit — a −33% vs −55% max drawdown —
  is insurance bought with forgone return, not a paycheck.
